evidence.requirements: Every requirement in the brief is met. The three tastings are defined with the brief's data (shared/tastings.ts:10-32). The start page shows title, date and time, EUR price per guest and "<n> seats left" (HomePage.tsx:35-48, TastingFacts.tsx:22; screenshots/start.jpg). Each tasting has a "Book <title>" link (HomePage.tsx:54-56). The form has fields labelled Name, Email and Guests (1-8) and a "Book" button (BookingPage.tsx:141-189). The server refuses to overbook and puts the error on the Guests field (app.ts:110-121, store.ts:68-69). Errors appear next to the field (Field.tsx:41-49; screenshots/form.jpg). The confirmation shows the heading "Booking confirmed", the tasting, guests, total price and reference (BookingPage.tsx:23-70; screenshots/confirmation.jpg). /staff has a Password field and a Sign in button, and the password is read from STAFF_PASSWORD (StaffPage.tsx:58-72, index.ts:6). Staff see bookings grouped by tasting with name, email, guests and reference, plus a Cancel button that frees the seats (StaffPage.tsx:78-141, store.ts:78; screenshots/staff.jpg). The stack is React with Express, React Router, react-hook-form, Zod and Tailwind. PORT defaults to 3000 (index.ts:5). Data is held in memory and the interface is in English.
evidence.correctness: Checking capacity and inserting the booking happen in one synchronous step (store.ts:65-76), so concurrent requests cannot oversell. api.test.ts:146-153 confirms this: 10 parallel requests produce exactly one 201. Boundaries are handled: exactly the seats left is accepted, one more is refused (api.test.ts:138-144). Guests of 0, 9, 2.5, a string or null are rejected by one shared Zod schema (shared/booking.ts:18-22). Name and email are trimmed. Unknown tastings and __proto__ return 404 (api.test.ts:124-128). Cancelling deletes the record, so seats are freed and a second cancel returns 404, which the UI handles gracefully (StaffPage.tsx:165-166). A ref guard plus the disabled button stops double submits (BookingPage.tsx:83,101). Fully booked tastings hide the form (BookingPage.tsx:226-239). Times show the winery's local wall-clock time regardless of the viewer's timezone (format.ts:19-26). Minor gaps: there is no confirm step before Cancel, and the confirmation disappears on reload.
evidence.security: React escapes all output and there is no dangerouslySetInnerHTML. The password check is constant time: both values are SHA-256 hashed and compared with timingSafeEqual. If the password is unset or empty, sign-in is disabled entirely (auth.ts:9-12). Sessions use random 32-byte tokens kept on the server with an 8-hour expiry, and sign-out destroys the token on the server (auth.ts:20-47, app.ts:160-164). The cookie is HttpOnly and SameSite=Strict, with Secure available via env (app.ts:145-151). Failed logins are rate-limited (app.ts:74-82). The server only accepts JSON, with 10kb/1kb body limits (app.ts:31-34,95,139). Helmet sets a strict CSP, the API sends Cache-Control: no-store, and the error handler hides internals (app.ts:198-208). The public API never exposes guest data (app.ts:92). No secrets are in the code; .env.example holds only a placeholder. One small gap: 'trust proxy' is not configured, so behind a reverse proxy all clients would share one rate-limit bucket.
evidence.code_quality: The code is cleanly split into shared/ (data, schema, formatting), server/ (app factory, auth, store) and src/ (pages, components, api, hooks). createApp is dependency-injected (store, clock, limits), which keeps it testable. Result types are discriminated unions (store.ts:14-17). Errors are handled by kind: field, network and server (api.ts:33-69, BookingPage.tsx:106-120). Names are clear and comments explain why rather than what (store.ts:41-45). TypeScript runs in strict mode with noUncheckedIndexedAccess. There is minor dead code: GlassIcon is never used (Icons.tsx:37-42).
evidence.tests: Vitest covers the shared schema, the store, the API through Supertest, and components tested against the real Express app (tests/helpers/harness.tsx). Playwright runs end to end on desktop and phone viewports with axe accessibility checks, overflow and touch-target checks, and a keyboard-only booking. Every brief requirement has a test: seats left (home.test.tsx:15-46), Book links, field errors including 0, 9, 2.5 and empty (booking.test.tsx:95-103), capacity and fully booked (booking.test.tsx:116-129,165-171), concurrency (api.test.ts:146), the confirmation contents, staff auth including fail-closed and expiry (api.test.ts:206-240), grouping, and cancel freeing seats (staff.test.tsx:94-106). test-results/.last-run.json shows a pass.
evidence.ux_design: The screenshots show a coherent winery identity: a serif display font, wine and cream palette, logo, date tiles, and green, amber and red seat badges (start.jpg). Errors are clear, with a red border, tinted background, icon and message under the field (form.jpg). The confirmation is distinct, with a green header and a highlighted reference box (confirmation.jpg). The staff overview is tidy, showing seats booked per tasting and an empty state (staff.jpg). The form shows a live total. The fully booked state has its own badge and copy. Phone layout is covered by the 360px e2e project. Small gaps: Cancel takes effect immediately with no confirmation, and the footer still says "Staff sign-in" when staff are already signed in.
evidence.accessibility: Labels are wired to inputs, errors use aria-invalid and aria-describedby, and errors carry a screen-reader "Error:" prefix (Field.tsx:22-49). Focus moves to the first invalid field (BookingPage.tsx:112) and to the confirmation heading (BookingPage.tsx:25,30). Notices use role=status and role=alert (Feedback.tsx, StaffPage.tsx:195). There is a skip link, focus moves to main after navigation (Layout.tsx:11-27), and focus outlines are visible (styles.css:49-53). lang="en" is set, document titles change per page, targets are at least 44px, and reduced motion is respected. The e2e suite asserts zero axe WCAG 2.2 AA violations on every page (quality.spec.ts:89-106).
evidence.simplicity: There are about 1,000 lines of app code with no exotic dependencies. Each library is an established one the brief encourages (Express, React Router, react-hook-form, Zod, TanStack Query, Tailwind). Helmet, express-rate-limit, the custom Permissions-Policy header, the session store and the fetch-stub harness with its cookie jar (harness.tsx:30-47) go somewhat beyond what a three-tasting site strictly needs, but each piece is small.
evidence.maintainability: The README explains run, dev and test commands, env variables, architecture and known limits (README.md). OpenSpec capability specs document the behaviour, regression tests are thorough, a lockfile is present, and TS config is strict. Gaps: there is no CI pipeline config at all. There are no ADRs or design notes; the README points to the openspec change 'winery-tasting-bookings' (README.md:41), which is not in the repo. There is no changelog or release/versioning approach beyond "version": "1.0.0". The Node runtime is not pinned (engines ">=22", no .nvmrc), and dependencies use caret ranges. There is no staff manual beyond two README lines, and the in-memory data loss on restart is only listed as a limit.

strengths: Correct, race-safe booking logic (store.ts:65-76) with one shared Zod schema validating identically on client and server, field-level errors and capacity errors on the Guests field.
Solid staff security: constant-time password check, fails closed when unset, server-side expiring sessions, HttpOnly/SameSite=Strict cookie, login rate limiting, CSP and JSON-only body limits.

A polished, coherent winery design with clear error, success and fully booked states and strong accessibility, backed by thorough unit, API, component and Playwright tests (including axe and phone viewport).
issues: Maintainability gaps: no CI pipeline, no ADRs (the openspec change cited in README.md:41 is missing), no changelog or versioning approach, Node not pinned (engines ">=22", no .nvmrc), and no real staff manual.
Bookings live only in memory: a server restart silently deletes every guest booking, which is risky for a live winery. It is documented as a limit, but no backup or file-based persistence is offered.

Staff Cancel takes effect immediately with no confirmation step (StaffPage.tsx:125-133), and rate limiting has no 'trust proxy', so behind a reverse proxy all clients share one login and booking limit bucket.
review.verdict: This is a well-engineered, accessible and visually polished booking app that meets every requirement in the brief, with correct seat handling, sound staff security and an unusually thorough test suite. Before shipping to the winery I would add a CI pipeline, pin the runtime, add a confirm step for cancellations and decide whether in-memory storage is acceptable. None of these block a first release.
